mainTopic: Throwing a גט between a roof and a courtyard: when the air counts as her guarded domain, how domains are divided for a גט, and how גיטין differ from שבת
overview: The משנה teaches that a גט thrown up to a wife on the roof works once it enters the roof's airspace. If the husband is on the roof and throws it down to her, it works once it leaves the roof, even if it is erased or burned before landing. The גמרא asks how air can count as a guarded place. It answers with a railing (מעקה) or the גט being within three טפחים of the roof for the first case, and with lower walls that stick out past the roof for the second case. Several אמוראים repeat that last answer and explain that even the רבנן, who argue with רבי about objects in the air on שבת, agree here, because a גט only needs to be guarded. רב נחמן limits the erased and burned cases: the writing must be erased on the way down, and the גט must be thrown before the fire started. רב חסדא rules that separate areas count as separate domains for a גט. רבא tries to prove this from the משנה by reading it as one place the husband lent her, but רמי בר חמא shows the proof does not hold. Finally רבא lists ways גיטין differ from שבת: for a גט, what matters is that it is guarded, so a גט on top of a tall reed does not work even though that spot counts as a private domain for שבת.

steps.title: משנה: wife on the roof, husband throws the גט up
steps.stepSummary: If the wife stands on the roof and the husband throws the גט up to her, she is divorced once it reaches the roof's airspace.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was standing on top of the roof and he threw the גט to her, once it reached the air of the roof, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that a גט thrown up to the wife on her roof works as soon as it enters the air above the roof, even before it lands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her roof counts like her own property, so the air above it can receive the גט for her. The גט does not need to actually land or reach her hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Airspace, the air above a place

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If she was standing on top of the roof
and he threw it to her,
phrases.notes: "It" is the גט, and the husband is standing below.

phrases.english: once it reached the airspace of the roof,
she is divorced.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט thrown up to the wife on her roof divorces her once it enters the roof's airspace.

steps.title: משנה: husband on the roof, wife below
steps.stepSummary: If the husband is on the roof and throws the גט down to the wife below, she is divorced once it leaves the roof's area, even if it is then erased or burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was above and she was below and he threw it to her, once it left the area of the roof, even if it was then erased or burned, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite setup: now the גט travels downward, and it works the moment it leaves the roof's area and enters the air of her space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The divorce takes effect while the גט is still in the air. So if it is erased or burned before it lands, the divorce has already happened and stays in force.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the divorce takes effect at the moment the גט enters her area. What happens to the גט afterward does not matter.

phrases.english: If he was above and she was below,
and he threw it to her,
once it left the area of the roof,
even if it was erased or burned,
phrases.notes: This means it got erased or burned on the way down, before it landed.

phrases.english: she is divorced.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט thrown down from the roof divorces her once it leaves the roof's area, even if it is destroyed before landing.

steps.title: But the roof's air is not protected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first case: the air above a roof is not a guarded place, so how can it receive the גט for her?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not guarded!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ruling of the משנה. A person's property only receives things for her if it is a guarded place, and the air above a roof does not seem guarded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wind could blow the גט away from the roof, so the roof's air looks like an unguarded area. An unguarded area cannot receive the גט for her, so why is she divorced?

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is that the roof isn't hers. The question is only whether the air above it is a protected spot, since a person's area receives things for her only when it is guarded.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But it is not guarded!
phrases.notes: The wind could carry the גט off the roof, so the air there isn't a protected spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first case of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that she is divorced once the גט reaches the roof's airspace
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a guarded area receives things for its owner. Air that the wind can blow the גט out of is not guarded.

steps.title: Answer: the roof has a railing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the משנה is talking about a roof with a מעקה (railing).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: we are dealing with a roof that has a railing.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by narrowing the case: the roof has a railing around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A railing keeps the גט from being blown off the roof. That makes the roof's air a guarded place, so it can receive the גט for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A railing or low wall around a roof
We are dealing with (a specific case)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
We are dealing with a roof that has a railing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The roof's air is open to the wind and unguarded
steps.terutzMaskana: With a railing, the גט cannot blow away, so the air counts as guarded

steps.title: Another answer: within three handbreadths of the roof
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר מנשיא in the name of אבימי says the case is when the גט is within three טפחים of the roof, which counts as the roof itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר מנשיא said in the name of אבימי: here we are dealing with the גט being less than three handbreadths from the roof, because anything less than three handbreadths from the roof is like the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not need a railing. Under the rule of לבוד, something less than three טפחים from a surface counts as if it is on that surface. So the גט is treated as lying on the roof, not floating in open air.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule that a gap of less than three טפחים counts as closed

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain the first case: שמואל says the roof has a railing, and אבימי says the גט is within three טפחים of the roof, so it counts as on the roof.

phrases.aramaic: עוּלָּא בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דַּאֲבִימִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Ulla bar Menashya said in the name of Avimi:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה סָמוּךְ לַגַּג עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with less than three, close to the roof,
phrases.notes: "Three" means three טפחים (handbreadths), measured from the גט to the roof.

phrases.english: since anything less than three close to the roof
is considered like the roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דַּאֲבִימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 3, different from שמואל's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case using the rule of לבוד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט is in open, unguarded air
steps.terutzMaskana: Within three טפחים, the גט counts as on the roof itself

steps.title: Same challenge on the second case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second case of the משנה and asks again: the air below is not guarded either.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He was above': but it is not guarded!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second case of the משנה and raises the same problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גט falls from the roof into her area below, the wind could still blow it out of her area. So how can that air already count as her guarded place?

phrases.english: 'He was above':
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the second case of the משנה (step 2).

phrases.english: But it is not guarded!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same challenge as step 3 to the משנה's second case
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that she is divorced once the גט leaves the roof's area
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The air of her area below can also lose the גט to the wind, so it is not guarded.

steps.title: Answer: the lower walls stick out past the upper ones
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the case is when the walls below extend further out than the walls of the roof above.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for example, when the lower walls stuck out beyond the upper ones.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers by narrowing the case: the walls of her area below are wider than the building above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lower walls stick out past the roof's walls, a גט falling from the roof must land inside her walled area. So its fall is guarded, and the divorce works as soon as it leaves the roof.
steps.whatToRemember: Both cases of the משנה only work when the air is truly guarded: by a railing or by being within three טפחים (first case), or by lower walls that stick out further than the roof (second case).

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For example, where the lower walls
stuck out beyond the upper ones.
phrases.notes: Picture the walls below standing further out than the roof's edge, so anything dropped from the roof falls inside them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ מְחִיצוֹת הַתַּחְתּוֹנוֹת עוֹדְפוֹת עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט could blow out of her area on the way down
steps.terutzMaskana: The lower walls stick out, so the גט must land inside her area and its fall is guarded

steps.title: More rabbis give the same explanation about the lower walls
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא, and עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן, both agree with שמואל's explanation: the lower walls stick out beyond the upper ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא, and עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the case is where the lower walls extend beyond the upper walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two more rabbis who explain the second case of the משנה exactly the way שמואל did in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the case itself. What is new is the support: the same answer comes from more chains of teachers, which shows it was widely accepted. Because the lower walls stick out, the falling גט passes through air that is enclosed by her courtyard walls.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said: introduces another rabbi who says the same thing
The lower ones (the walls of the courtyard below)
The upper ones (the walls of the roof above)

phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Elazar
in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
For example, where the lower walls
extend beyond the upper ones.
phrases.notes: So the גט falls inside the line of the yard's walls the whole way down.

phrases.english: And so said Ulla
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
For example, where the lower walls
extend beyond the upper ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 7 with more sources that say the same thing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second case of the משנה is where the lower walls extend beyond the upper walls.

steps.title: Does this follow only רבי's view about objects in the air?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks עולא whether this explanation depends on רבי's opinion that an object caught in the air counts as if it was put down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rabbi Abba said to עולא: Whose view is this? Is it רבי's view, who said that an object caught in the air is treated as if it was set down?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא asks עולא which earlier opinion this explanation is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט is still falling through the air when it counts as given. That sounds like רבי's rule from the laws of שבת, that an object in the air of a place counts as if it landed there. If so, the רבנן, who argue with רבי, might not agree with this explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה
Caught in the air: an object still in the air inside a space
Is treated as if it was set down

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Ulla:
Like whom? Like Rabbi?
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name always means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: who said: an object caught in the air,
is treated as if it was set down?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְעוּלָּא: כְּמַאן, כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which earlier opinion the lower-walls explanation depends on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the explanation work only according to רבי's rule of קלוטה, or also according to the רבנן?
steps.kashyaTarget: The lower-walls explanation given by עולא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it depends on רבי's rule, it would not fit the רבנן who disagree with him.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree, because the גט is guarded
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that even the רבנן agree here, since they argue with רבי only about שבת. For a גט, what matters is that it is guarded, and it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You can even say it follows the רבנן. The רבנן disagree with רבי only regarding שבת. But here, the reason is that it is guarded, and it is guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רבי אבא: this explanation works even according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, the question is whether the object really 'rested' in a new place, and the רבנן require it to truly land. For a גט, the question is different: is it in a protected space that belongs to her? Between her own walls the גט is already protected, so she is divorced even before it lands.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן
They only disagree up to this point (and no further)

steps.whatToRemember: A גט needs to be in a guarded place of hers. It does not need to 'land' the way an object must land for the שבת laws.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two topics. The argument between רבי and the רבנן is about carrying on שבת, not about גיטין.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same physical situation can be judged differently depending on what each area of law cares about.

phrases.english: He said to him: You can even say the Rabbis
The Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi
regarding Shabbat;
but here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case of giving a גט.

phrases.english: it is because of being guarded,
and it is guarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's question from step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It fits even the רבנן, since their argument is only about שבת. For a גט, being guarded is enough.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between areas of law (שבת versus גיטין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The explanation seemed to need רבי's rule that an object in the air counts as resting.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט only needs to be guarded, so even the רבנן agree.

steps.title: רבי אסי gives the same explanation in רבי יוחנן's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן, also says that the case is where the lower walls extend beyond the upper ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן: the case is where the lower walls extend beyond the upper walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more rabbi who taught the same lower-walls explanation. This sets up a second, parallel question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another chain of teachers bringing the same answer from רבי יוחנן. The גמרא repeats it because a different rabbi will now ask this teacher the same question about whose opinion it follows.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Asi
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
For example, where the lower walls
extend beyond the upper ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another source for the same explanation, setting up a parallel question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is where the lower walls extend beyond the upper walls.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי the same question
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי whether this explanation follows רבי's view that an object caught in the air counts as set down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Whose view is this? Is it רבי's view, who said that an object caught in the air is treated as if it was set down?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי the same question that רבי אבא asked עולא. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the same as in step 9: does the explanation depend on רבי's rule of קלוטה? This time it is asked of רבי אסי, and step 13 gives his answer.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who asks רבי אסי the question

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
Like whom? Like Rabbi?
who said: an object caught in the air is treated as if it was set down?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי: כְּמַאן, כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks רבי אסי the same question that was asked of עולא in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אסי's explanation depend on רבי's rule of קלוטה?
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it depends on רבי's rule, the רבנן who disagree with him might not accept it.

steps.title: רבי אסי answers that even the רבנן agree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא with the same reasoning עולא gave: the רבנן argue with רבי only about שבת. For a גט, what counts is that it is guarded, and it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You can even say this follows the רבנן. The רבנן argue with רבי only about שבת. But here the reason is that the גט is guarded, and it is guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא's question from the last step. He says the explanation does not depend on רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שבת, the question is whether an object in the air counts as 'resting', and there the רבנן disagree with רבי. For a גט, she only needs the גט to be guarded inside her domain. Air inside her walls is guarded, so everyone agrees.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same wording as עולא's answer in step 10. The גמרא repeats it because a second, separate exchange (רבי זירא and רבי אסי) ended the same way.

phrases.english: He said to him: You can even say the Rabbis —
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי אסי, answering רבי זירא.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי,
phrases.english: the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi
phrases.notes: Literally 'until here the Rabbis only disagree': it limits how far their argument goes.

phrases.english: only with regard to Shabbat;
but here, it is because of being guarded,
and it is guarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'lower walls stick out' explanation needs רבי's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Even the רבנן agree, because a גט only needs to be guarded, and the air inside her walls is guarded.

steps.title: Erased on the way down, not on the way up
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה limits the משנה's case of an erased גט. She is divorced only if the writing was erased while the גט was coming down. If it was erased while still rising, she is not divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'erased': רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: They taught this only when it was erased on the way down. If it was erased on the way up, she is not divorced. Why? At first, it was not yet set to land there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, a גט that was erased in the air. רב נחמן says this rule only works when the גט was already falling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that once the גט left the roof's domain, she is divorced even if it got erased. רב נחמן adds a limit. A גט still going up could be blown somewhere else, so it does not yet count as landing in her domain. Only once it is coming down is it treated as already there.

phrases.english: "Was erased":

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְחַק דֶּרֶךְ יְרִידָה,
phrases.english: They taught this only when it was erased on the way down,
but if it was erased on the way up, no.
What is the reason?
At first, it is not set to come to rest there.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְחַק: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the walls discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Erasing does not stop the divorce only if it happens on the way down. If it happens on the way up, she is not divorced.

steps.title: Burned only counts if the גט came before the fire
steps.stepSummary: Using the same pattern, רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says a burned גט still divorces only if it was thrown before the fire started. If the fire was already there, she is not divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'burned': רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: They taught this only when the גט came before the fire. If the fire came before the גט, she is not divorced. Why? From the start it was heading to be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the same thing for the next line of the משנה, a גט that burned in the air. The rule only holds if the fire started after the גט was thrown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גט was thrown into a fire that was already burning, it was headed for destruction from the very start. So it is as if he never really gave her a גט. If the fire only started later, the גט had already counted as in her domain.
steps.whatToRemember: Both limits follow one idea. The גט counts as already in her domain only if, when it was thrown or while it was moving, it was really heading to land there. A גט still rising, or thrown into a fire that was already burning, was not.

phrases.english: "Was burned":

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁקָּדַם גֵּט לִדְלֵיקָה,
phrases.english: They taught this only when the bill of divorce preceded the fire,
but if the fire preceded the bill of divorce, no.
What is the reason?
From the start it is heading toward burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׂרַף: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same speaker and same pattern as step 14, applied to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A burned גט still divorces only if it was thrown before the fire started. If the fire came first, she is not divorced.

steps.title: Separate areas are separate domains for a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא states a new rule: domains are divided when it comes to גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Domains are divided with regard to bills of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens a new topic with a short rule about domains in the laws of גיטין. The גמרא is setting up a discussion of what this rule means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the סוגיא asked whether the גט reached her domain. רב חסדא adds that, for a גט, different areas, like a house and a courtyard, are each treated as their own domain. They are not all lumped together as one.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
Domains are divided with regard to bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רְשׁוּיוֹת חֲלוּקוֹת בְּגִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about domains, after the משנה's details were explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For גיטין, different areas count as separate domains.

steps.title: What is the source for רב חסדא's rule?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רבא where רב חסדא, called 'the Elder,' learned that domains are divided for גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said to רבא: Where does the Elder get this rule from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking for the source of רב חסדא's rule from Step 16. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said domains are divided in גיטין, but he gave no source. רמי בר חמא wants to know what text this rule is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elder; here it means רב חסדא
From where does he know it? A request for a source

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said to Rava:
From where does the Elder get this?
phrases.notes: 'The Elder' is רב חסדא, and 'this' is his rule from the last step that domains are divided for גיטין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב חסדא's rule stated in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source supports the rule that domains are divided for גיטין?

steps.title: רבא points to the משנה about the roof
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the source is our משנה: if she stands on the roof and he throws the גט up to her, she is divorced once it reaches the roof's airspace.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is our משנה. If she was standing on top of the roof and he threw the גט to her, once the גט reaches the airspace of the roof, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says the source is the משנה and quotes the case of a wife standing on a roof. He will now analyze this case to prove the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on the moment the גט enters the roof's airspace. רבא will ask why that exact moment matters. The answer will depend on who owns the roof and who owns the courtyard.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is our משנה:
If she was standing on top of the roof
and he threw it to her,
phrases.notes: He is standing below, throwing the גט up toward her.

phrases.english: once the גט reaches the airspace of the roof,
she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by naming the משנה as the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the משנה of the wife standing on the roof, where the גט works once it reaches the roof's airspace.

steps.title: If the roof and courtyard are both hers, why wait for the roof?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what case the משנה describes. If both the roof and the courtyard are hers, the גט should work as soon as it is in her courtyard, so the roof's airspace should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say her roof and her courtyard, why do I need the airspace of the roof?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts testing who owns the roof and who owns the courtyard. He rules out the first option: that both belong to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט lands in the wife's own property and divorces her. If the courtyard were hers too, the גט would already work while it is in the courtyard. So the משנה's focus on the roof makes no sense in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say; it opens a possibility that is about to be tested
Why do I need it? It points out that something seems unnecessary

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say with her roof and her courtyard,
why do I need the airspace of the roof?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts analyzing the case in the משנה quoted in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that both the roof and the courtyard belong to her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the courtyard were hers, she would be divorced before the גט reached the roof, so the roof's airspace would not matter.

steps.title: If the roof and courtyard are both his, the roof should not help
steps.stepSummary: The second option fails too. If both the roof and the courtyard are his, reaching the roof's airspace changes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his roof and his courtyard? When it reaches the airspace of the roof, what of it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries the opposite option: both belong to the husband. He rules this out as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everything belongs to him, the גט never leaves his own property. A גט that is still in his domain cannot divorce her, so reaching the roof would mean nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?
Rather; it moves on to a new possibility

phrases.english: Rather, with his roof and his courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הִגִּיעַ לַאֲוִיר הַגָּג מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: when it reaches the airspace of the roof, what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out 'both hers,' this tests and rules out 'both his.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that both the roof and the courtyard belong to him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט still inside the husband's own domain cannot divorce her, so reaching the roof should not help.

steps.title: The first part of the משנה must mean her roof and his courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The only case that fits is that the roof is hers and the courtyard is his. That explains why the גט works only once it reaches the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious: her roof and his courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the first part of the משנה. The roof belongs to her and the courtyard belongs to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the גט passes through his courtyard, it is still in his domain. Once it enters the airspace of her roof, it is in her domain and she is divorced. Next, רבא checks whether this setup also fits the last part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; here, the only option left

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious:
with her roof and his courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With both other options ruled out, this states the case that works.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The roof and the courtyard might belong to the same person.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the first part of the משנה, the roof is hers and the courtyard is his.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה does not fit the same setup
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the last part of the משנה. He is on the roof and she is below, and the גט works once it leaves the roof even if it is erased or burned. If the roof were hers and the courtyard his, that ruling would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last part: He is above and she is below, and he threw it to her. Once it left the area of the roof, even if it was erased or burned, she is divorced. And if it is her roof and his courtyard, why is she divorced?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא checks the last part of the same משנה against the setup he just reached. He shows that it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the גט falls from the roof down into the courtyard. If the courtyard were his, the גט would be entering his own domain, so leaving the roof could not divorce her. The setup that worked for the first part fails for the last part.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part of the משנה
Domain; the area someone owns or controls

phrases.english: Say the last part:
He is above and she is below
and he threw it to her;
once it left the area of the roof,
if it was erased or burned,
phrases.notes: This means it was erased or burned in the air, before it reached the ground.

phrases.english: she is divorced.
And if it is her roof and his courtyard,
why is she divorced?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the setup from Step 21 against the last part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the setup 'her roof, his courtyard' to the last part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט falling from the roof into his courtyard stays in his domain, so leaving the roof should not divorce her.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה must mean his roof and her courtyard
steps.stepSummary: For the last part to work, the roof must be his and the courtyard hers. Once the גט leaves his roof, it is in her domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is his roof and her courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא concludes that the last part of the משנה would have to describe the opposite ownership: his roof and her courtyard. This sets up his objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גט leaves his roof, it enters the airspace over her courtyard, which is her domain. So she is divorced even if the גט is destroyed before it lands. The result, though, is that the first part and the last part of the משנה describe opposite ownership setups. The next step finds that hard to accept.
steps.whatToRemember: So far: first part of the משנה, her roof and his courtyard; last part, his roof and her courtyard. רבא is about to question whether one משנה would switch setups like this.
steps.confusionAlert: This split reading is not רבא's final view. In the next step he finds it hard to accept, and he replaces it with a single case where the husband lent her one place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This two-setup reading is the possibility רבא rejects in step 24. רמי בר חמא later revives it in step 26 to knock down the proof.

phrases.english: Rather, with his roof and her courtyard;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem in Step 22 by switching who owns the roof and who owns the courtyard in the last part of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case (switching who owns what)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last part of the משנה has the same setup as the first: her roof and his courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last part of the משנה describes his roof and her courtyard.

steps.title: Can the two halves of the משנה be different cases?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the רישא and the סיפא would be describing opposite ownership setups without saying so.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it really be that the first part is about a roof that is hers and a courtyard that is his, while the last part is about a roof that is his and a courtyard that is hers?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that steps 21 and 23 forced the two halves of the משנה into opposite cases. He finds it hard to believe that one משנה would switch cases without saying so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 needed the roof to be hers and the courtyard his. Step 23 needed the opposite. A משנה that silently flips the facts halfway through seems unlikely, so רבא will look for one case that fits both halves.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה

phrases.english: The first part is about a roof that is hers and a courtyard that is his,
and the last part is about a roof that is his and a courtyard that is hers?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא בְּגַג דִּידַהּ וְחָצֵר דִּידֵיהּ, סֵיפָא בְּגַג דִּידֵיהּ וְחָצֵר דִּידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of steps 21 and 23 together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the רישא and the סיפא describe opposite ownership cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single משנה is not expected to change its facts silently between its two halves.

steps.title: Everything is his, and he lent her one spot
steps.stepSummary: Both halves describe one case: the husband owns both the roof and the courtyard and lent her one place, because people lend only one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that he lent her a place? People lend one place; people do not lend two places.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives one case that fits both halves. Both the roof and the courtyard belong to the husband, and he lent her just one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא he lent her the roof, and in the סיפא he lent her the courtyard. Either way, the גט works only once it reaches the spot he lent her, because people normally lend only one place. This shows that a roof and a courtyard count as separate places for a גט, which is the point רב חסדא wanted to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that... (introduces the reading being argued for)

steps.whyThisMatters: If this reading holds, the משנה proves that different areas owned by one person can count as separate places for a גט.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that he lent her a place?
For people lend one place,
but people do not lend two places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's proof for רב חסדא (asked for in step 17). It gives one case that fits both halves after step 24 rejected splitting them.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so that one setup explains both halves.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves describe opposite ownership cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything belongs to the husband, and he lent her one spot. That spot is the only place where she can receive the גט.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה really does describe two different cases
steps.stepSummary: The reply rejects the proof: each half can be its own case, roof hers and courtyard his in the רישא, and the opposite in the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is that a proof? Maybe each part is as it is. The first part is a roof that is hers and a courtyard that is his, and the last part is a roof that is his and a courtyard that is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers רבא that his proof does not work. The משנה can describe two different cases, one in each half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's proof depended on the idea that one משנה cannot switch cases. The reply says it can, so there is no need for the 'lent place' reading. Without that reading, the משנה no longer proves that a roof and a courtyard count as separate places.

keyTerms.meaning: Are the cases really comparable? Is that a proof?
This one as it is, and that one as it is: each case stands on its own

steps.confusionAlert: This reply does not prove the opposite view. It only shows that this משנה cannot be used as proof either way.

phrases.english: He said to him: Are the cases comparable?!
phrases.notes: This is רמי בר חמא, answering רבא.

phrases.english: Perhaps this one is as it is, and that one is as it is:
the first part is about a roof that is hers and a courtyard that is his,
and the last part is about a roof that is his and a courtyard that is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in step 25 by accepting the possibility raised in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה that a roof and a courtyard count as separate places.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes a משנה cannot describe two different cases. In fact, it can.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from this משנה falls away, because each half can be read as its own ownership case.

steps.title: רבא's first special rule for a גט: airspace
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists three ways גיטין differ from שבת. The first: the dispute between רבי and the רבנן about whether an object in the air counts as resting applies only to שבת. For a גט, all that matters is that it is protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are three special rules in גיטין. The first is this. רבי said that an object caught in the air counts as if it were resting, and the רבנן disagree with him. That dispute applies only to שבת. Here, though, the question is whether the גט is protected, and it is protected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new teaching listing three ways the rules of a גט differ from the rules of שבת. This step gives the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שבת, רבי and the רבנן argue about whether an object in the air counts as having landed. For a גט, landing is not the question at all. What matters is whether the גט is protected inside her area, and once it is inside her airspace it is protected, so even the רבנן agree it works.

keyTerms.meaning: Three special rules or ways of measuring
Something caught in the air counts as if it were resting

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a גט works on a different basis from שבת. For a גט the question is protection, not whether the object has come to rest.

phrases.english: Rava said: There are three special rules in bills of divorce.
phrases.notes: He means three ways the rules of a גט differ from the rules of שבת.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי: קְלוּטָה כְּמִי שֶׁהוּנְּחָה,
phrases.english: That which Rabbi said, 'An object caught in the air counts as resting,'
and the Rabbis disagree with him on it:
that applies only to Shabbat.
But here, it depends on whether it is protected,
and it is protected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new teaching by רבא that compares גיטין with שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a גט, whether an object in the air counts as resting does not matter. If the גט is protected in her airspace, it works, and even the רבנן agree.

steps.title: רב חסדא's rule: a basket on a tall reed counts as a private domain
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב חסדא's שבת ruling. If someone throws an object onto a basket sitting on top of a reed that stands in a רשות היחיד, he is חייב even if the reed is a hundred אמות tall, because a רשות היחיד reaches up to the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is the ruling of רב חסדא: someone stuck a reed into the ground of a private domain, and there was a basket on top of it. He threw something from outside and it landed on the basket. Even if the reed is a hundred אמות high, he is liable, because a private domain goes all the way up to the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second item on רבא's list. He first quotes a known שבת ruling of רב חסדא so that in the next step he can explain why it does not carry over to a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, carrying from a רשות הרבים into a רשות היחיד is forbidden. The height of the spot does not matter: anything above a private domain is still part of it, so the basket on the reed counts as inside the private domain. That is why the thrower is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: stuck a reed into the ground

phrases.english: And there is what רב חסדא said:
If someone stuck a reed into the ground of a private domain
and on its top was a basket,
and he threw something and it came to rest on top of it,
phrases.notes: He throws from the public domain into the private one.

phrases.english: even if the reed is a hundred אמות high, he is liable,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד עוֹלָה עַד לָרָקִיעַ –
phrases.english: because a private domain goes up all the way to the sky.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's list from Step 27 with the second difference between גיטין and שבת, starting by quoting the שבת rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, an object landing on a basket atop a reed in a רשות היחיד makes the thrower חייב at any height, because a רשות היחיד extends up to the sky.

steps.title: For a גט, what counts is protection, and a tall reed does not protect it
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רב חסדא's rule to שבת. A גט works only when it is protected in her domain, and a גט sitting on top of a tall reed is not protected, so she is not divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies only to שבת. But here, with a גט, the reason it works is that it is protected, and a גט up on the reed is not protected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives the actual difference. רב חסדא's rule is about שבת, but a גט follows a different test: is it protected?
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, the question is only which domain the object is in, and a private domain goes up without limit. A גט thrown into her domain divorces her only because her domain keeps it protected for her, like her hand would. A גט on top of a tall reed is not protected (it is not secured there), so even though it is in her domain for שבת, it does not divorce her.
steps.whatToRemember: The same spot can count as her domain for שבת and still fail for a גט, because a גט needs to be protected, not just located in her domain.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the reed's top stops being a רשות היחיד. It is still her domain. The point is that a גט needs more than that: it must also be protected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a גט placed in a woman's domain works on the basis of protection, like her hand holding it, and not on the שבת idea of domains.

phrases.english: this applies only to the laws of שבת,
but here, it works because the גט is protected,
and this one, up on the reed, is not protected.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת, אֲבָל הָכָא מִשּׁוּם אִינְּטוֹרֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the שבת rule quoted in Step 28 and applies the protection test from Step 27 to a גט on a tall reed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא's rule applies only to שבת. A גט resting on a tall reed in her domain does not divorce her, because it is not protected.
